events.title: Burnt relics represented years of digs
events.text: THE Glamorgan/Gwent Archaeological Trust are still counting the cost of the disastrous fire which swept through their Swansea warehouse last Sunday evening destroying thousands of relics of Welsh heritage.

events.quote: the most rapacious ground landlord, Western Ground Rents, has been bought by the BP pension fund, which is behaving in the same rapacious and, at times, unfeeling and uncaring way in handling the genuine requests of householders.
src: Hansard, HC Deb 22 May 1980, vol. 985 (Legal Wiki EV-0057)

events.title: Housing Bill: Amendments of Leasehold Reform Act 1967 etc.
events.text: Mr. Edward Rowlands (Merthyr Tydfil): “We have had some cranky and curious ground landlords in South Wales, but the saddest aspect is that the most rapacious ground landlord, Western Ground Rents, has been bought by the BP pension fund, which is behaving in the same rapacious and, at times, unfeeling and uncaring way in handling the genuine requests of householders. Such ground landlords are prompting the growing demand for further amendments to the 1967 Act. I should like to think that if the many pensioners in the BP fund realised that it was using its power to drive harsh bargains with householders and to act tough and without feeling or care, they would not want such actions to be taken in their name. It is regrettable that a distinguished company, which is half owned by the Government, should behave in that way.”

events.title: Historical Society had notable year
events.text: […] Following the business of the meeting, members were given a fascinating talk by Mr. Henry Owen-John, the assistant director of the Glamorgan/Gwent Archaeological Trust. The subject of his lecture, which was illustrated by numerous slides, was the work of the Trust and some of their recent archaeological ‘digs’ in Glamorgan, notably the excavations at Llandough near Cardiff, where the substantial remains of a Roman Villa and part of a later medieval house were discovered.

events.title: Letter: Grievous loss
events.text: SIR,—The proposal for the ultimate demolition of the Great House Farm, Llandough, would unwittingly erase from memory one of the early historical sites of Glamorgan, marking, as it does, the location of the ancient Celtic monastery, a centre of first importance in the rise of Christianity in Morgannwg, comparable, indeed, in early record with the two other great Celtic monasteries of St. Cadoc at Llancarfan and of St. Illtyd at Llantwit Major.

events.quote: But I will refuse to move because not only is this my home it is part of the nation’s heritage

events.title: ‘Open day’ to save ancient Welsh house
events.text: HUNDREDS of people yesterday flocked to see an 800-year-old house, containing centuries-old furniture and china, which is in danger of being demolished by developers.

events.text: Mrs. M D. Buckler was objecting to further industrial development in the vicinity of her farm, Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough. Land farmed by her family since 1667 had been “wrongfully appropriated.”

events.text: London Gazette, 31 October 1958, p.6652: notice of the Minister’s intention to lay before Parliament “the City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order, 1957, confirmed by him on the 8th September 1958, under section 5 of the Physical Training and Recreation Act, 1937”.

events.title: City wants common for play-field
events.text: Mrs. Mary Doreen Buckler, of Great House Farm, Llandough, said she did not oppose the proposal so long as it applied only to playing fields. About 130 years ago Lord Bute allowed her family “a slice of land” which was now Leckwith Common.

events.text: Leckwith Woods … “bought … for a nominal sum in 1942” … “outside the boundary” …

events.title: “Bought … for a nominal sum in 1942”: 106 acres leased to the Forestry Commission
events.text: The Western Mail of 18 March and 28 October 1955 reports Cardiff holding a 176-acre Leckwith Woods “bought … for a nominal sum in 1942”, 106 acres leased to the Forestry Commission for 999 years, and Leckwith Woods described as “outside the boundary”.

events.title: Surrender and new yearly tenancy, as the Court of Appeal recites it
events.text: The Court of Appeal recites a surrender of the earlier tenancy and a new yearly tenancy to Frederick Buckler on 2 February 1949; the intended written tenancy “did not happen because Mr Frederick Buckler also failed to pay the rent”. It then recites a High Court possession order (2 February to 4 July 1955) and a Cardiff County Court possession order of 11 December 1962.

events.title: The gift of Leckwith Woods is completed
events.text: “The Council acquired a part of Leckwith Woods comprising some 109 acres as a gift from Western Ground Rents Ltd, which had bought the urban estate of the Bute family in 1938. The gift was offered and accepted in 1940, though the transfer of ownership was not formally completed until April 1942. The deed included a covenant that the land be used as a playing field, park, recreation or pleasure ground only.”

events.title: 5.30 acres “adjacent to Ty-Mawr farmhouse and Llwyn-yr-eryr”
events.text: Agreement, Western Ground Rents to John Williams, May 1939, with plan: 5.30 acres adjacent to Ty-Mawr farmhouse and Llwyn-yr-eryr (Glamorgan Archives DBDT123/7). The plan shows Parcel B only, highlighted.

events.title: The Bute interest at Llandough passes to Western Ground Rents Ltd
events.text: Conveyance of the Bute interest at Llandough to Western Ground Rents Ltd, dated 25 December 1938 in the 1965 contract for sale (condition F, root of title); the press reported completion on 23 December 1938. The deed’s plan, which would show exactly what land went, has not been found.

events.title: Trustee Act notice
events.text: “CHARLES SAINT DAVID SPENCER late of Llwyn-yr-eryr Llandough Juxta Penarth in the County of Glamorgan and of 6, Working Street in the city of Cardiff Deceased.” Two days later the paper reported his will: “solicitor, and formerly clerk to the Whitchurch Justices, of Llwyn-yr-Eryr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and of 6, Working-street, Cardiff, left everything to his widow”.

events.title: Llandough Bride
events.text: The wedding took place at Llandough Church of Mr. Fred Buckler, of Barry, and Miss Mary Doreen (Nancy) Williams, of Great House Farm, Llandough.

events.title: Offered at auction and withdrawn
events.text: “Messrs. Stephenson and Alexander (F.A.I) offered for sale at Cardiff on Thursday the leasehold residential property, Llwyn-yr-Eryr, Llandough near Cardiff, which was withdrawn, the reserve not having been reached. The solicitors were Messrs. Spencers.”

events.title: Signature on the Welsh Women’s Peace Petition: “Llandough”
events.text: Esther Williams is the eighth signature on page 1 of petition sheet 1/92; address “Llandough”, with no farm name. The other addresses on the sheet (Lewis Road, Cogan, Llwyn-yr-Eryr “Near Cardiff”) put it on the Penarth side.

events.title: Yearly agricultural tenancy of the whole farm
events.text: The Court of Appeal recites a yearly agricultural tenancy of the farm granted to John Williams in February 1916.

events.title: Court Leet at Llandough
events.text: The annual court leet and court baron of the lordship of Bute was held on Thursday week last at the Merry Harriers Hotel, Llandough … A vote of sympathy was passed with the family of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House, Llandough, for many years a juror of the court. In accordance with historic tradition, the presentments were signed by the deputy steward and jury.

events.title: Mr. John Williams, Great House

events.text: Conveyance, John Marquis of Bute to Cardiff City Corporation, 23 February 1905, as recorded on HM Land Registry title WA735527 (land lying on the Leckwith side).

events.title: The Bute rent audit
events.text: Amongst the Marquis of Bute’s guests at the rent audit dinner at Cardiff on Saturday was Mr John Williams, of Llandough Farm … He succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855 … Saturday was his 102nd rent audit.

events.title: “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)” in the Bute coppice-woods sale
events.text: Catalogue entry for the Bute coppice-woods auction of 29 November 1902, including “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)”. Whether the soil or only the timber and coppice rights were sold, to whom and on what terms, is not in the catalogue.

events.title: Wireless Telegraphy. Marconi Invention Tested at Lavernock
events.text: The postal authorities of the country have evidently faith in the possibilities of the Marconi system of telegraphing without wires, and the Italian inventor (M. Marconi) has reason to feel proud of the success of the demonstrations, so far as they have yet been carried out. M. Marconi, as was reported the other day, successfully carried out on Salisbury Plain a series of experiments with a couple of balloons attached by wires to the ground.

events.title: Swine fever at Llandough
events.text: Swine fever has broken out at Llandough and Rhoose this week. Five pigs belonging to Mr Williams, Great House, have been slaughtered. On Tuesday morning, one of a herd of 23 was reported as being affected, and it was feared that the whole would have to be slaughtered.

events.title: Geese case, Llandough
events.text: … the property of Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, on November 11, 1891 …

events.title: Llandough. [Reported] Farmyard Theft.
events.text: Robert Williams, a mason’s labourer, was on Tuesday charged (before Mr. John Duncan and Mr. J. S. Corbett) at the offices of the clerk to the Penarth magistrates, High-street, Cardiff, with stealing three geese, the property of Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, on November 11, 1891.—Sergeant Ferris, of the Cardiff Borough Police Force, deposed that he saw the prisoner early on the morning in question in Clive-street, Grangetown, carrying the geese on his back. He at once started after Williams, who dropped the geese and got away.—Police-constable Morgan, of the county constabulary, said he arrested the prisoner when he was leaving Cardiff Gaol on Monday. The prisoner, when charged with stealing the geese, replied, “All right.”—The prisoner was remanded until Monday at Penarth.

events.title: A Batch of Orchard Looters at Llandough
events.text: … four … boys … appeared in answer to the charge of breaking into the orchard of Great House Farm, on Sunday morning, and [taking] therefrom a number of apples, the property of John Williams … P.C. Herbert Evans said … with the assistance of Mr John Williams, junior, caught three of the offenders … The boys got into the orchard over the hedge from the railway … John Williams, junior, corroborated the evidence of the constable, and added that about half the apples in his father’s orchard had been [taken].

events.title: Agreement with the Marquess of Bute over land at Great House Farm
events.text: Agreement, Marquess of Bute to Daniel Thomas & Son, 1877. The Bute deeds at the National Library of Wales describe “land (33 a.), formerly part of Great House Farm, for the Llandough Limeworks (33 a.), 1876-1912”.

events.title: Amy Williams
events.text: The Williams / Buckler family announces the passing of Amy Williams, relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm. She died at Llandough, near Cardiff, on 23 December 1864, aged 65.
